h: Pendle pointers for a top climbing trip
p: Before you set off for The Leisure Box, run through this quick checklist and you'll be sorted.

Book a slot. Clip 'n Climb runs in timed sessions, and weekends and school holidays fill up fast. Fill in the forms. Every climber needs a participation form, signed by a parent or guardian for under-18s, and it's quickest done online. Check the ages. There's usually a minimum age for climbers and supervision rules for younger children, so read through them when booking. Allow time. Give yourselves a couple of hours for the whole visit, including the safety briefing and harness fitting.

And on the walls themselves? Start with the easy challenges to warm up, then move on to the timed races, and finish with the big jumps when everybody's feeling brave. Wear trainers and comfy clothes, bring water, and leave rings and watches behind.

Pendle has some cracking places to round off a day. The Pendle Heritage Centre in Barrowford, close to Brierfield, has a walled garden, displays about local history and a cafe. Wycoller Country Park, near Colne, is a gorgeous little valley with old packhorse bridges and the ruins of Wycoller Hall, often linked with the Brontës. Over in Burnley, Towneley Park is huge, with a historic hall, a museum and art gallery, plenty of walking paths and play areas. And if anyone fancies a proper hike, Pendle Hill's famous outline is never far from view.
